reader.requirement: At 1985 a program directly or indirectly contained in a program whose FD carries GLOBAL may reference that file-name (and its records) without describing it, and every such reference, in the container and in each contained program, operates on the one common file connector (open mode, position, record area, status); a non-global file, a sibling's global file or a contained program's global file is not visible, and a contained program's own same-named file is its own.

edition-consulted.switches: the GLOBAL clause in the linkage section is a 2002 construct (refused at 85); an FD's GLOBAL is not gated

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Dialect in InheritStep.cs and InheritedGlobals.cs: none; SymbolTable.InheritFiles walks every container (nearest first) and adds each GLOBAL FileModel to the contained unit's visible files at every edition; BinderDriver keys each connector by its declaring unit, so the contained program's verbs hold the container's FileModel and its one registry key
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness shares one global file between a container and one contained program; not exercised are an indirectly contained program, a READ position shared across programs, a CLOSE in a contained program, the refusal of a non-global or sibling's file, and a contained program's own same-named file

probes.printed: OUTER READ OUT01 / INNER READ MID02 FS=00 / OUTER READ DEP03 / AFTER INNER CLOSE FS=00 (MATCH)
probes.expected: writes by the container, a directly and an indirectly contained program land in one file in order; READ position is shared (inner reads record 2, outer then record 3); a CLOSE in a contained program closes the common connector

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: 'LREC' is not defined ... / error COBOL1639: 'LF' is not defined as a file ...
probes.expected: a container's file without GLOBAL is not visible in the contained program: refused

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: 'SF' is not defined as a file ...
probes.expected: a sibling's GLOBAL file is not declared in any program containing SBB: refused

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: 'UF' is not defined as a file ...
probes.expected: a contained program's GLOBAL file is not visible to its container: refused

probes.printed: OUTER WRITE FS=00 / OUTER FILE 1 OUTER / OUTER FILE 2 OUTR2
probes.expected: the contained program's own XF is its own connector (§1985:X.1.3.8): its write does not reach the container's global XF

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.1.3.7 GR2  (║1.3.7 Sharing Files║)  the text is in GR2
OK  §1985:X.1.3.8  (1.3.8 Scope of Names)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: Global file-names are inherited structurally (InheritStep walks every container and InheritFiles makes each GLOBAL FileModel visible), so the contained program binds to the container's own FileModel and the run time sees one connector; nothing on the path consults the edition. Every probed sharing and scope case behaved as the 1985 text requires.

refuter.evidence: Probed what the reader did not, at --std 85: (1) the intermediate program declares its own NON-global file XF and the outer one a GLOBAL XF; the innermost program's WRITE goes to the outer's connector (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/gx_midnonglobal.cob, runs/gx_midnonglobal-001: OUTER FILE 1 OUT01 / OUTER FILE 2 DEP02 / EOF3), as §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR1 puts only global names of containing programs in the set; (2) both outer and intermediate declare GLOBAL XF; the innermost program uses the intermediate's, the nearer one (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/gx_midglobal.cob: MID FILE 2 DEP02, outer file holds only OUT01); (3) a failed OPEN and the READ after it in a contained program set the container's non-global FILE STATUS item, and an OPEN in a contained program of a file the container opened gives 41 (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/gx_status.cob: AFTER INNER OPEN FS=35 / AFTER INNER READ FS=47 / OUTER OPEN OUTPUT FS=00 / INNER REOPEN FS=41); (4) an indexed GLOBAL file in DYNAMIC access: a contained START/READ NEXT, the container's READ NEXT continuing from that position, a contained REWRITE of the current record (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/gx_idx.cob, runs/gx_idx-003: INNER NEXT 002BBBB / OUTER NEXT 003CCCC / INNER REWRITE FS=00 / OUTER KEYED 002BBBB); (5) LINAGE-COUNTER of a GLOBAL LINAGE file advanced by a contained program's WRITE AFTER ADVANCING is the container's (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/gx_linage.cob, runs/gx_linage-002: OPEN LC=01 / INNER LC=04 / OUTER LC=04). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.1.3.7 GR2', 'OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR1'. One connector in every case.
